To anyone interested in playing but worried their computer won't be able to handle it:

You can run the game at half the resolution while still keeping the menus and UI at your desktop resolution. The game's low-poly style really does not suffer much at all by lowering the resolution. Obviously you'll be losing a bit of that crisp-ness, but once you get to playing none of that matters.

I was expecting this game to be whole from day 1 and stay that way. I'm expecting this game to go the direction that Insurgency went. Bought up by a big publisher only for them to lose vision of their game and bleed developers. The people who made Insurgency, New World Interactive, is now defunct. So I am expecting that from this. Either Tuxedo Labs will lose it's vision and just become another product pushing corporate developer or go defunct in little over a year. You can't have nice things I guess.

tl;dr: Game is great, don't expect publishers to treat it fairly, mods are awesome. 5/10

Imagine Minecraft got blackout drunk, snorted C4, and started screaming “EVERYTHING MUST GO!” That's Teardown. You’re a one-man wrecking crew with a fetish for destruction and a vendetta against architecture. Smash walls, torch trucks, launch pianos through windows, then leg it like MacGyver on bath salts. It’s criminal mischief meets precision speed-running in a world made of edible pixels. 11/10 — my therapist plays it to understand me.

Awesome game and great concept. Yes, the premise is silly considering the capers, but the destruction and creativity of the solutions are top notch.

"Teardown" is an absolute blast if you love creative destruction. The game's voxel-based world is fully destructible, letting you smash, crash, and blow up everything in sight. The physics are super satisfying, and planning heists where you have to think on your feet adds a nice strategic layer.

The sandbox mode is perfect for unwinding after a long day—there's something oddly therapeutic about reducing a building to rubble. It's a bit light on narrative, but honestly, who needs a story when you're having this much fun wrecking stuff?

If you enjoy games that let you unleash your inner demolition expert, "Teardown" is a must-play.

This game is fantastic. It's a essentially a puzzle game with voxel destruction. You have a task at hand, whether it is to steal art or blow something up, among other things. You have an unlimited setup phase where you can mold the map to your liking in order to make a great escape. Typically you will have to trigger an alarm that runs out in 1 minute. During that time you need to complete the objectives and escape before the police take you out. After finishing all the maps and not playing for a while, I just logged in and saw they add all new content. Totally worth the sticker price.

At first I was irritated by the timed objectives thinking this was just a "destruction-oriented" game. (If you're like me who hasn't read the game's description properly, this IS a Destruction-oriented game where you do HEISTS). I dropped it for about 5 months, and only recently came back to it. I finally get what the game is about and ever since I could not drop it for one bit. I MUST COMPLETE IT.

The game has two significant modes: Campaign and Sandbox.
-Campaign makes you do heists with progressive difficulty and weapon unlocks. (Even though this is a campaign, elements like how long the alarm rings can be adjusted with no repercussions, and more.)
-Sandbox is self-explanatory and I guess where most people are at.

Despite the time-oriented aspect of the Campaign, this has actually struck my brain the perfect way. I admire the puzzle aspect of it, the relaxing pace of strategizing, the freedom of options, the manly satisfaction of destruction, and the rewarding aspect of progress. I make it a point to finish all objectives!

TL;DR: Game is good. Campaign: Heist w/ Destruction, Sandbox: Destruction only. Campaign already scratch my itch to juggle brain a bit and destroy stuff. Good in Singleplayer, Good in Co-op. Please use quick-save often.

details.text: For someone buying now, the recent score is about the same as the all-time one, and fewer recent reviews raise bugs and crashes.
